transcript.content: Hi, welcome in. To start off, could you tell me what brings you in today?

Well, I'm here because... for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern in my project files at work. I'm a translator, and certain subcontractors, along with one colleague in particular, keep making these tiny changes to the translation memory and the timestamps. 

They're doing it so it looks like my quality control failed. I've brought it up at work, and even though IT says the audit trail is completely clean... I know what I'm looking at. I know the record has been arranged to put the blame on me. It's been causing me a lot of stress, so I figured I should come in and talk to someone.
Besides noticing these changes in your files, have you ever heard, seen, or sensed things that others around you didn't seem to notice—like hearing voices or sounds that others couldn't hear?

No, nothing like that. I don't hear voices or... see things that aren't there, if that's what you mean. My hearing and vision are perfectly fine. 

What I'm dealing with is strictly on my computer screen. I'm looking at actual data, you know? It's not my imagination or my senses playing tricks on me. It's just those specific translation files being altered.
You mentioned this has been going on for months—can you tell me exactly how long you've held this belief that your colleague and subcontractors are altering the files to blame you?

Well, I wouldn't really call it a belief, since it's just what's happening in the data. But... to answer your question, it's been going on for about 11 months now. 

It started shortly after I was put in charge of the new localization project at work. That's when I first began noticing the discrepancies in the files.
Outside of this work situation, do you generally find yourself distrustful or suspicious of other people's motives—like friends, family, or people you don't know well?

No, not at all. I mean, my friends and family... we get along fine. I don't have any reason to doubt their motives or anything like that. I'm not a naturally suspicious person, if that's what you're asking. 

Outside of the office, my life is completely normal. I trust the people close to me, and I don't have issues with strangers, either. It's really just this specific situation at work with the translation memory and those specific people. That's the only place I'm having this problem.
Have you noticed any recent changes in your memory, concentration, or overall thinking, or do you have any medical conditions, head injuries, or substance use that started around the time this began?

No, nothing like that. My memory and focus are the same as they've always been. I don't have any medical conditions, and I haven't hit my head or anything. I don't use drugs, and I only drink occasionally, like a beer with dinner on the weekends. My mind is perfectly clear. Like I said, the only thing going on is what's happening with the files at work.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with a single, fixed, non-bizarre persecutory delusion (belief that colleagues/subcontractors are altering file data/timestamps to frame him) persisting for approximately 11 months. There are no hallucinations, no disorganized speech or behavior, no negative symptoms, and no mood episode symptoms reported. Functioning outside the specific delusional theme (relationships with friends/family, general trust, cognitive function) remains intact, and there is no evidence of a general pattern of pervasive suspiciousness (ruling out paranoid personality disorder) or an underlying medical/substance-induced etiology. The circumscribed nature of the delusion, preserved reality testing in unrelated domains, and duration >1 month are consistent with Delusional Disorder, Persecutory Type (F22.0). Schizophrenia (F20.0) is excluded due to absence of hallucinations, disorganization, or negative symptoms and preserved functioning; unspecified psychosis (F28) is less specific given the clear delusional syndrome criteria are met.
